articles.title: Zeiss expands German site that caps ASML's EUV scanner output — first new building opens four years after Oberkochen site groundbreaking
articles.text:
Zeiss expands German site that caps ASML's EUV scanner output — first new building opens four years after Oberkochen site groundbreaking
ASML's 2025 annual report stated that its lithography tool output is limited by Carl Zeiss SMT's capacity.
Zeiss Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology has confirmed that it's adding around 25,000 square meters of production and production-adjacent space at Oberkochen in southern Germany, with staff moving into the first completed building this month, four years after the 2022 groundbreaking. The remaining buildings will be handed over in stages. Oberkochen and Wetzlar are the only two places in the world where the optical columns inside ASML's lithography scanners can be built, and ASML's own annual report states that the number of systems it can produce is limited by Zeiss SMT's production capacity. ASML told investors earlier this month that it plans to lift Low-NA EUV output by roughly 30% in 2027.
ASML's 2025 annual report describes Carl Zeiss SMT as its sole supplier of lenses, mirrors, illuminators, collectors, and other critical optical components, held under an exclusive arrangement. If Zeiss couldn't sustain production over a prolonged period, the filing warns, ASML "would effectively cease to be able to conduct our business." Purchases from Zeiss SMT and its subsidiaries reached €4.41 billion in 2025, up from €3.95 billion in 2024 and €3.33 billion in 2023. (1 Euro = 1.14 USD)
CFO Roger Dassen said during ASML's July earnings call that it's close to fully booked on Low-NA EUV for 2027, is raising capacity by about 30% from roughly 65 systems this year, and is evaluating another 30% increase for 2028. He told reporters the same day that the company is compressing its scanner build cycle from around 22 weeks to 15 or 16. It's understood that ASML is planning Low-NA EUV machine price hikes, something which has reportedly upset TSMC.
High-NA projection optics contain more than 40,000 parts and weigh about 12 tons, roughly seven times the volume and weight of standard EUV optics. The illumination system adds another 25,000 parts and 6 tons. Individual High-NA mirrors weigh several hundred kilograms, around twice the size and 10 times the weight of current EUV mirrors, and Zeiss says they're machined for months before reaching the required figure. Verifying them requires a purpose-built vacuum chamber measuring 5 by 10 meters, made up of over 100,000 parts and weighing more than 150 tons. Intel became the first company to ship high-volume logic on 0.55 NA scanners this month. Adding floor space doesn't shorten any of those steps.
ASML held €1.91 billion in loans receivable from Zeiss SMT at the end of 2025, up from €1.44 billion a year earlier, alongside €1.19 billion in advance payments made to secure optical column deliveries. Two €1 billion facilities are in place, signed in September 2021 and September 2024, and ASML issued a further €444 million loan in July 2025 and a €212.5 million short-term loan in November. A May 2025 restatement of the company's framework agreement made the capex loans interest-free, with repayment expected over seven or 15 years and quarterly installments that vary with Zeiss SMT's revenue.
Zeiss SMT booked €5.055 billion in the fiscal year to September 30, 2025, up 23% and the largest of the Zeiss Group's four segments. It's also building a multifunction factory at Wetzlar, added 300 square meters of cleanroom at Rossdorf last fall, and opened an innovation center in Korea this month.

articles.title: Este es el mejor ajuste de Android Auto que te recomiendo activar
articles.text:
Android Auto es una maravilla, pero no es perfecto. Si llevas tiempo utilizándolo, sabrás que Google tiene que mejorar algunas zonas de la interfaz, aunque también es posible que no conozcas uno de los ajustes ocultos más útiles del servicio. Se activa solo una vez, tardas menos de un minuto y ni siquiera necesitas estar en el coche para dejarlo listo. ¿Qué hace? Incluye un pequeño widget en la interfaz para poder manipular la música u otras apps cuando el GPS oculta toda la pantalla.
La gracia es no tener que cambiar de aplicación para cambiar de canción, pausar o saber qué tema está sonando. Todo esto se comprime en un pequeño widget que se ubica en la parte inferior y que se va a convertir en tu cosa favorita de Android Auto. De hecho, es tan bueno que muchos piensan que debería llegar al servicio por defecto.
Activarlo es muy fácil, pero debes saber dónde está la opción, porque de lo contrario es probable que nunca llegues a toparte con ella o a saber que algo así existe para mejorar la experiencia de Android Auto. Por suerte, hoy estás en el lugar correcto. Te vamos a contar dónde está, cómo se llega y, por supuesto, cómo activarlo.
Y, aunque se puede desactivar si no te gusta, ya te adelantamos que se va a quedar para siempre en la pantalla de tu coche.
Así se activa el widget oculto de Android Auto
Cuando esté activo, este widget mostrará una pequeña ventana en la parte inferior de la pantalla en la que se muestra el estado de la aplicación secundaria. Es decir, si estás en el GPS se mostrará Spotify, y si estás en Spotify verás información del GPS. Todo sin tener que poner la pantalla dividida y pudiendo tener acceso interactivo para no tener que saltar de aplicación en aplicación y perder la vista principal.
Para activarlo solo tienes que seguir estos pasos desde tu móvil. Ojo, no se activa estando en el coche, por lo que puedes hacerlo ahora mismo, dejarlo activado y que se muestre cuando conectes el dispositivo a tu vehículo.
- Abre los ajustes de tu móvil
- Busca 'Android Auto'
- Baja hasta la opción 'Widget de la barra de tareas'
- Actívalo y listo
Ahora se mostrará siempre que conectes tu móvil al coche y tengas una app secundaria ejecutándose, como la música o el GPS. Y, por supuesto, se puede activar en cualquier móvil, marca o versión de Android.

articles.title: The US is charging an American citizen for wiping his phone at the border
articles.text:
The government is prosecuting US citizen Sam Tunick for allegedly providing authorities with a “duress password” that wiped his phone when they tried to seize it at Atlanta’s Hartsfield-Jackson airport on January 24th, 2025. Federal agents detained Tunick at the airport, allegedly questioning him about child exploitation images. However, a motion filed by Tunick’s lawyers argues this was simply “a pretext for a fishing expedition into Mr Tunick’s connections” to the Stop Cop City movement in Atlanta.
The US is charging an American citizen for wiping his phone at the border
Sam Tunick allegedly gave federal agents a fake ‘duress password’ at the airport.
Sam Tunick allegedly gave federal agents a fake ‘duress password’ at the airport.
The government is turning to a little-known and rarely-used statute that makes it illegal to destroy or damage property to stop authorities from seizing it. They allege that Tunick used a feature of the privacy-focused GrapheneOS to wipe his phone by giving authorities a duress password, instead of the actual passcode to unlock the phone. The defense has argued that the detention and seizure were unlawful, and therefore all evidence should be tossed.
According to Tunick’s attorneys, agents refused him access to a lawyer, did not provide a warrant, or inform him of his legal rights. They also allege that access to his phone was sought under false pretenses. The government has countered that they were not required to produce a warrant because Tunick had not yet been granted permission to enter the US.
Marlon Kautz, a member of the Atlanta Solidarity Fund, told the Guardian earlier this week that, “we all have a right to secure our private data against unconstitutional searches. And we should — especially in a time of rising authoritarianism.” Under the Trump administration, entering the US has become a much more fraught process, even for citizens who can face hours-long detention and scrutiny of social media accounts. Most agree the only way to protect your data is to delete it.

articles.title: Why more Australian businesses are ditching in-house IT for managed service providers - Tech Guide
articles.text:
For years, having an in-house IT person, or a small internal team, was simply how growing businesses handled technology. Lately, though, more Australian businesses are quietly making the switch to managed service providers instead, and the reasons behind that shift go well beyond just cutting costs.
It reflects a broader change in how businesses think about technology altogether, from something managed reactively to something treated as a core part of how the business runs day to day.
Predictable costs beat unpredictable emergencies
One of the biggest drawcards is cost certainty. A single in-house IT hire comes with a fixed salary regardless of how much or how little support is needed in any given month, while unexpected outages or hardware failures can blow out budgets fast. Managed providers typically work on a fixed monthly fee, which makes IT spending far easier to forecast and removes the nasty surprise invoices that so often come with reactive, break-fix support. For a growing business trying to plan a budget twelve months ahead, that predictability alone can be worth the switch, since it turns IT from a wildcard expense into a known, manageable line item.
Access to a broader bench of expertise
A single internal IT person, however capable, is still just one person with one set of specialisations. Networking, cyber security, cloud infrastructure and help desk support all require different skill sets, and few individuals are genuinely strong across all of them. A managed provider brings a whole team with varied expertise, meaning a business gets access to specialists it could never justify hiring individually. This matters more than it might seem at first glance, since a growing business’s technology needs rarely stay simple for long, and having access to a wider bench of knowledge means problems get solved properly the first time, rather than patched together by someone stretching outside their comfort zone.
Less downtime, faster resolution
When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, a lone in-house IT worker might already be stretched thin or simply unavailable. Managed providers are built around fast response times and often round-the-clock monitoring, catching problems before they escalate into full outages. For a business that depends on its systems being up and running, that difference in responsiveness can matter enormously. Many providers also use proactive monitoring tools that flag early warning signs, such as a server running low on disk space or a device showing signs of failing, well before those issues turn into a full outage that stops the business in its tracks.
Security is no longer optional
Cyber threats have become more sophisticated and more frequent, and keeping pace with patching, monitoring and best practice requires ongoing attention that a lot of internal teams simply don’t have the bandwidth for. Managed providers build security into their day-to-day operations rather than treating it as an occasional project, which matters given how quickly the threat landscape continues to shift. This includes everything from routine patch management to monitoring for suspicious activity across a network, tasks that are easy to let slip when there’s only one internal person juggling every other IT responsibility at the same time.
It’s not just for large enterprises anymore
This shift isn’t limited to big corporates with deep pockets. Smaller and mid-sized Australian businesses are increasingly turning to providers such as MSP Blueshift to essentially act as their entire IT department, scaling support up or down as the business grows without the overhead of building an internal team from scratch. For many owners, this also removes the ongoing headache of recruiting, training and retaining IT staff in a tight labour market, replacing it with a single, predictable relationship that grows alongside the business.
The move away from in-house IT isn’t about businesses no longer valuing good technology support. If anything, it’s the opposite: as technology becomes more central to daily operations, more business owners are recognising that a dedicated, specialised team can deliver a level of support that a single internal hire, however good, simply can’t match on their own.

articles.title: Gandalf arrive sur Les Anneaux de Pouvoir, où s'asseoir en IMAX pour l'Odyssée, le recap Pop Culture !
articles.text:
Les Anneaux de pouvoir va enfin avoir le vrai Gandalf tant aimé des fans
- La troisième saison de la série Les Anneaux de Pouvoir promet une montée en tension avec l’ascension de Sauron et l’entrée en scène du vrai Gandalf.

IMAX : où s’asseoir pour ne pas gâcher L’Odyssée de Nolan (mon expérience au Pathé Île Seguin)
- Assis en rangée D, la proximité de l’écran oblige à baisser les yeux pour lire les sous-titres, ce qui fait systématiquement manquer une portion de l’image et altère légèrement la géométrie IMAX.
- L’Odyssée de Christopher Nolan est précisément le type de production pensée pour l’immersion de cette salle IMAX et y livre le choc visuel attendu.

- Prévue le 25 décembre 2026 sur HBO et Max, la série Harry Potter avance « à marche forcée », un marathon logistique qui fait travailler des centaines de techniciens dans l’ombre pour tenir le calendrier.

articles.title: Norton 360 Deluxe passe à 39,99 € la première année : 5 appareils protégés et VPN illimité inclus (-63 %)
articles.text:
La suite antivirus Norton 360 Deluxe tombe à 39,99 € la première année au lieu de 109,99 €, soit 70 € d'économie sur une suite qui couvre 5 appareils, avec VPN illimité inclus, gestionnaire de mots de passe et surveillance du dark web. La formule deux ans descend à 89,99 € au lieu de 219,99 €.
Avec près de 33 % des demandes d'assistance et une hausse de 71 % en un an, l'hameçonnage reste de loin la première menace visant les particuliers, selon le rapport d'activité 2025 de cybermalveillance.gouv.fr.
C'est le terrain de Norton 360 Deluxe, qui regroupe antivirus, VPN et surveillance des données personnelles dans une seule application. Notre test de la suite Norton 360 lui attribue 9,3/10 et en fait notre solution préférée pour la famille.
Cinq appareils couverts pour 3,33 € par mois
Le socle, c'est le moteur antivirus, et il tient ses promesses : sur les tests Windows d'AV-Test de mai et juin 2025, Norton bloque 100 % des 407 échantillons zero day et des 19 213 échantillons collectés sur la période, sans le moindre faux positif. L'impact sur les performances de la machine reste par ailleurs contenu, ce qui n'a pas toujours été le cas chez l'éditeur.
Autour de ce noyau, la Deluxe ajoute Norton VPN sans limite de volume, un gestionnaire de mots de passe, le Dark Web Monitoring qui alerte dès qu'une adresse mail ou un numéro de carte apparaît dans une fuite, SafeCam, 50 Go de sauvegarde cloud et le contrôle parental Norton Family.
Tout savoir avant de choisir Norton 360 Deluxe
Le VPN illimité est l'argument fort de l'offre, mais notre test en tempère la portée. Norton annonce plus de 3 000 serveurs pour une couverture de seulement 29 pays, le choix du protocole n'est pas proposé, WireGuard est absent, et il ne s'agit pas d'un VPN no log.
NortonLifeLock étant établi en Arizona, il relève du Patriot Act et des alliances des 5, 9 et 14 Eyes. Pour sécuriser un Wi-Fi public, c'est largement suffisant.
Notez également que SafeCam est réservée aux PC et la version Mac ne dispose pas de la sauvegarde en ligne.
✅ Les points forts

articles.title: Redenschreiber ChatGPT: Schadet KI unserer Kommunikation?
articles.text:
ChatGPT als Redenschreiber? Was gute Kommunikation aus Sicht einer Kommunikationsberaterin braucht
Wir sind unsicher, wie viel künstliche Intelligenz in der Kommunikation erlaubt ist. Das zeigt die Debatte um Beiträge von Politikern und Journalisten, die mit KI erstellt worden sein sollen. Franzi von Kempis berät Unternehmen und Organisationen zu genau diesem Thema. Im Podcast t3n Arbeit in Progress teilt sie ihr Einschätzungen zur Auswirkungen von KI in der Kommunikation.
Generell hat sie dazu eine klare Position: „Der Mensch muss am Anfang stehen, in der Mitte stehen und am Ende stehen.“ KI könne ein Sparringspartner sein, der beim Strukturieren und Überarbeiten hilft. Doch die Kernaussage müsse immer von einem Menschen kommen. Das gilt besonders, wenn es um Haltung, Meinung oder politische Versprechen geht.
KI fehlt Gefühl für die Zwischentöne
Kempis selbst nutzt KI etwa nicht für ihren Newsletter, denn sprachlich würde die Leistung nicht ausreichen. Laut der Kommunikationsberaterin neigen KI-Chatbots wie ChatGPT etwa zum „klassischen Dreiklang“, bei dem eine Aufzählung mit drei Teilen erfolgt.
Außerdem schließt sie sich der Aussage von Anne-Kathrin Gerstlauer gegenüber t3n an: Ein schlechter Text bleibe ein schlechter Text. Der KI fehle Sprachgefühl und ein Verständnis für die Zwischentöne, die Menschen in Reden und Texten teilen.
Drei Punkte für gute Kommunikation
Für die Kommunikationsberaterin macht gute Kommunikation drei Punkte aus. Erstens musst du wissen, was du sagen willst. Du brauchst also eine klare Aussage. Zweitens muss der Adressat klar sein. Alle zu erreichen ist kein passendes Ziel, da dies ohnehin nicht gelingen könnte.
Drittens musst du dir des „Wie“ bewusst sein. Gerade in Zeiten von Fake News und Propaganda sei es wichtig, Botschaften emotional und kreativ zu transportieren, ohne dabei populistisch zu werden. Was ihr zentrale Rat für den Umgang mit KI in der Kommunikation ist und welche Zukunftsperspektiven sie in dem Bereich sieht, teilt Kempis in der verlinkten Episode.
Podcast t3n Arbeit in Progress anhören
Ihr könnt den Podcast t3n Arbeit in Progress bequem in der Podcast-App eurer Wahl abonnieren. In der Regel findet ihr den Podcast einfach über die Eingabe „t3n Arbeit in Progress“ in der Suche. Ansonsten könnt ihr auch den RSS-Feed manuell in der App eingeben.

articles.title: Piloter son PC avec la langue : un étonnant accessoire à 1400 dollars arrive sur le marché
articles.text:
Pendant des années, contrôler un ordinateur sans les mains exigeait de choisir entre deux mauvaises options : la dictée vocale (très pratique pour rédiger un email, nettement moins pour naviguer dans un tableur ou sélectionner un calque dans Photoshop), et le suivi oculaire (précis, mais avec une caméra infrarouge vissée sous l’écran et un prix à faire soupirer). Augmental, startup californienne née au MIT Media Lab, a cherché une troisième voie du côté de la bouche.
Le MouthPad est un capteur palattal (un appareil discret que l’on glisse derrière les molaires supérieures, à mi-chemin entre la gouttière orthodontique et le périphérique Bluetooth) qui lit les mouvements de la langue via une surface tactile et les traduit en commandes ordinateur. Un glissement déplace le curseur. Une pression déclenche un clic. Les gestes de la tête complètent la navigation. La connexion est sans fil, le dispositif invisible de l’extérieur, silencieux. Disponible dès maintenant aux États-Unis, à 1 400 dollars.
MouthPad is a touchpad you drive with your tongue.
Now available across the US. pic.twitter.com/n8Gvq2Y37Q
— Augmental (@augmentaltech) July 22, 2026
Des premiers utilisateurs aux ventes publiques : le MouthPad change de terrain
Présenté pour la première fois au grand public lors du CES 2024, le MouthPad a surtout circulé pendant deux ans dans les couloirs des hôpitaux et des centres de rééducation. Ses utilisateurs cibles : des patients atteints de sclérose latérale amyotrophique (ALS), des personnes paraplégiques, tétraplégiques ou en phase de récupération post-AVC. Les non-verbaux constituent une autre cible centrale : pour une personne qui ne peut ni parler ni taper, la surface tactile palatale ouvre des possibilités que les autres interfaces ne permettent pas. Tomás Vega, cofondateur d’Augmental, résume l’ambition en une formule assez directe : « la technologie doit aller là où se trouvent les humains, et non l’inverse. »
L’ouverture aux ventes publiques s’accompagne d’un second produit : Vox, un accessoire vocal complémentaire (200 dollars, actuellement en bêta, livraison prévue fin 2026) qui superpose une couche de contrôle par la voix au-dessus du capteur palatal. Pour les personnes qui peuvent vocaliser mais pas naviguer, ou l’inverse, l’idée est un système hybride combinant les deux modalités. Le marché n’est pas anecdotique. Environ 1,3 milliard de personnes dans le monde, soit une sur six, vivent avec un handicap significatif, dont une large part ne dispose pas encore d’un dispositif d’assistance numérique adapté.

articles.title: Station complète et puissance de 25 000 Pa : cet aspirateur robot laveur passe sous la barre des 400 €
articles.text:
Face à Roborock et Dreame, Ecovacs reste un poids lourd incontournable du marché des aspirateurs-robots. Le Deebot T50 Omni Gen 3 se positionne comme le modèle accessible de la gamme 2026 du constructeur chinois, juste en dessous du T50 Pro Omni Gen 3 qui ajoute la surveillance vidéo et une batterie plus généreuse. On retrouve ici l’essentiel : une puissante aspiration, un nettoyage 2-en-1 avec doubles serpillières rotatives et une station tout-en-un. Un ensemble complet, d’autant plus intéressant avec cette remise de 100 euros chez Boulanger.
Ce qu’il faut retenir de l’Ecovacs Deebot T50 Omni Gen 3
- Son format plat de 81 mm, idéal sous les meubles bas
- Une station avec vidange, lavage et séchage automatiques
- Sa puissance d’aspiration de 25 000 Pa et ses serpillières rotatives
Proposé initialement à 499 euros, l’Ecovacs Deebot T50 Omni Gen 3 est en ce moment proposé en promotion à 399 euros chez Boulanger.
Un robot qui se faufile partout
Avec ses 81 mm de hauteur, le Deebot T50 Omni Gen 3 fait partie des robots les plus compacts du marché. Son petit gabarit lui permet de se glisser sous la plupart des canapés, lits et meubles bas sans rester coincé. C’est en grande partie grâce au repositionnement de son capteur LiDAR dToF, directement intégré dans le châssis, ce qui évite la tourelle habituelle qui dépasse sur certains concurrents.
Le nettoyage 2-en-1 combine aspiration et lavage en un seul passage grâce à ses doubles serpillières rotatives. Ecovacs a aussi prévu un système de levée automatique des serpillières jusqu’à 9 mm lorsqu’un tapis est détecté, avec quatre modes de gestion dédiés. La puissance d’aspiration grimpe à 25 000 Pa sur cette Gen 3, contre 21 000 Pa sur la génération précédente : il ne devrait rien laisser sur le sol.
La navigation TrueDetect 3D lui permet de longer les meubles de près et de couvrir les bords efficacement. En revanche, on reste sur un système moins avancé que celui du modèle Pro, ce qui peut se traduire par un contournement d’obstacles un peu moins efficace, au risque de s’y cogner.
Une station qui gère (presque) tout à votre place
C’est sur la station que ce Deebot T50 Omni Gen 3 tire une bonne partie de son intérêt. Elle se charge de vider le bac à poussière dans un sac de 3 litres, de laver les serpillières à l’eau chaude à 75 °C, de les sécher à l’air chaud à 45 °C et de recharger automatiquement le détergent.
Côté autonomie, Ecovacs annonce environ 2 heures et 50 minutes de fonctionnement, ce qui permet de couvrir des logements de bonne taille. Un vrai gain, même si les logements très grands avec beaucoup de tapis pourraient bénéficier de la batterie plus endurante du modèle Pro (6 400 mAh contre 5 200 mAh ici).
Si vous souhaitez comparer l’Ecovacs Deebot T50 Omni Gen 3 à d’autres références du marché, nous vous invitons à consulter notre guide des meilleurs robots aspirateurs pour trouver celui qui correspond le mieux à vos besoins et à votre budget.

articles.title: La "revolución" de la IA va por barrios: el mapa que muestra quién manda y quién se ha quedado fuera
articles.text:
Cuando la IA llegó y vimos todo lo que podía hacer, la primera impresión de muchos fue que les iba a quitar el trabajo (y la verdad, algunas declaraciones tampoco ayudaron), aunque la realidad de momento es otra: trabajamos más y descansamos menos. Saber usar la IA se ha convertido en una skill más, una que puede ser esencial en función de tu trabajo: no es lo mismo ser camarera que secretaria ni ser fontanero o periodista.
Pero incluso aunque la profesión importa y los despliegues más o menos globales (de hecho, Europa suele quedarse atrás por cuestión de legislación), la IA no ha calado igual en todo el mundo. El Microsoft AI Diffusion Report que monitoriza la economía de la IA a escala global (concretamente, 100 países) para el primer trimestre de 2026 recoge un hecho: el 17,8% de la población mundial en edad laboral la usa, pero hay 10 países que la lideran y muchos que van a la cola.
Eso sí: el informe de Microsoft usa telemetría anonimizada de sus productos. Es decir, si alguien usa solo ChatGPT, Gemini o Claude y nunca toca nada de Microsoft, no aparece en el recuento. Microsoft intenta corregir ese sesgo con ajustes estadísticos, pero no lo elimina del todo.
El informe de Microsoft se ve mejor con esta adaptación a infografía de Visual Capitalist que colorea los países en función de su uso de la IA: los tonos amarillos para aquellos lugares con alta adopción y los morados donde se usa poco. Es, en pocas palabras, una fotografía cuantitativa del uso real de herramientas de IA generativa.
Es inevitable asociar la adopción de la IA con la productividad laboral y la competitividad. Sin ir más lejos, la propia Microsoft lo hace relacionando sus efectos reales en el empleo: el trabajo de dev en EEUU batió récords en 2025, llegando a los 2,2 millones, un 8,5% más que el año anterior. Obviamente, esta brecha entre los países que más usan la IA y los que menos tienen como trasfondo el acceso desigual a esta tecnología. En pocas palabras: es una brecha digital más que perpetua y amplía las desigualdades que ya existen.
Qué países lideran el uso de la IA
Entre los países que lideran el uso de la IA destaca uno: Emiratos Árabes Unidos, con un 70% de su población en edad de trabajar usando inteligencia artificial y un crecimiento que cuadriplica el ritmo promedio mundial. Le siguen Singapur (63%) y un grupo de países muy digitalizados mayoritariamente europeos: Noruega (49%), Irlanda y Francia (48% cada uno), España (44%), Nueva Zelanda (43%), y Reino Unido, Países Bajos (42%). Cierra el top 10, Catar empatado con los Países Bajos. El patrón es claro: son economías moderadamente ricas, con buena conexión a internet y gobiernos que llevan años invirtiendo en infraestructura digital.
Pero la inmensa mayoría se mueve muy por debajo de esas cifras y qué mejor ejemplo que un a priori inesperado Estados Unidos: solo tiene un 31% de cuota pese a ser la cuna de todopoderosas como Gemini de Google, Claude de Anthropic o ChatGPT de OpenAI. Una cosa es construir inteligencia artificial y otra muy diferente, usarla. Aquí depende más de tener una infraestructura digital homogénea, políticas estatales de adopción y igualdad territorial, factores donde los estados pequeños como EAU o Singapur tienen ventajas estructurales.
En la cola están muchos países de África, Asia Central y Latinoamérica, con cuotas de apenas un dígito o poco más: Venezuela 10%, Rusia 10%, Marruecos 12%, Bolivia 13%, entre otros. La brecha digital entre el norte y el sur, en su máxima expresión: el Norte Global llegó al 27,5% de uso frente a solo el 15,4% del Sur Global. La IA se extiende, pero de forma heterogénea hacia aquellos que ya iban adelantados en digitalización.
No obstante, cabe recordar nuevamente que al basarse en telemetría de productos de Microsoft, este indicador puede subestimar la adopción real en mercados donde predominan otros proveedores: mención especial merece China, donde el ecosistema de IA tiene productos locales potentes como Baidu, Alibaba, Deepseek o Moonshoot y su impresionante Kimi K3.
En Xataka | Quién está ganando realmente la carrera de la IA, en un gráfico que pone en aprietos a Google
Portada | Visual Capitalist

articles.title: MIT’s new lidar chip could give self-driving cars a wider view
articles.text:
MIT’s new lidar chip could give self-driving cars a wider view
New breakthrough could help create smaller and more durable sensors for vehicles, drones, and industrial sites.
- Date:
- July 22, 2026
- Source:
- Massachusetts Institute of Technology
- Summary:
- MIT engineers have found a way to give chip-based lidar a wider, clearer view without relying on moving parts. Their design uses differently shaped antennas that can sit close together without scrambling one another’s signals. In tests, the system sharply reduced interference while steering a single precise beam across a broad field of view.
- Share:
Lidar technology uses pulses of infrared light to calculate distances and create detailed 3D maps of the surrounding environment. This allows autonomous vehicles to detect objects in their path and respond quickly. However, conventional lidar sensors are often large and costly, and many rely on moving components that can wear out over time. These limitations make the systems difficult to use in a wider range of settings.
MIT researchers have now developed an approach that could lead to smaller, more durable lidar sensors that operate without any moving parts. Their advance centers on a new silicon-photonics chip, a type of semiconductor device that controls light instead of electrical signals.
Existing lidar systems built with silicon-photonics chips usually have a narrow field of view. As a result, they struggle to scan areas located toward the edges of a scene. Previous attempts to expand this viewing range have often introduced extra noise and reduced measurement accuracy.
The MIT team addressed those problems by creating an array of integrated antennas that greatly limits unwanted crosstalk, which occurs when neighboring antennas interfere with one another. The design allows the chip to scan across a broader field of view while producing less noise than other silicon-photonics-based methods.
A Smaller Lidar System With a Wider View
The advance could support the development of more capable lidar sensors for challenging uses, including autonomous vehicle navigation, aerial mapping, and the monitoring of construction sites.
"The functionality we demonstrated in this work solves a fundamental problem for integrated optical-phased-array technology, enabling future lidar sensors that can achieve significantly higher performance than we could demonstrate previously," says Jelena Notaros, the Robert J. Shillman Career Development Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) at MIT, a member of the Research Laboratory of Electronics, and senior author of a paper on this innovation.
The study also includes lead author and EECS graduate student Henry Crawford-Eng, along with EECS graduate students Andres Garcia Coleto, Benjamin M. Mazur, Daniel M. DeSantis, and Tal Sneh. The findings were published recently in Nature Communications.
How Lidar Maps Its Surroundings
Many traditional lidar systems use a large rotating unit to direct light pulses across a scene. When the light strikes nearby objects, it reflects back toward the sensor. The returning signals provide the information needed to reconstruct a detailed map of the environment.
Silicon-photonics-based lidar works differently. Rather than rotating a mechanical device, it scans a beam of light electronically in several directions with a system known as an integrated optical phased array (OPA).
At the heart of an OPA is a group of integrated antennas. Each antenna contains tiny, regularly spaced variations along its length. These features, known as corrugations, cause light from an input source to scatter upward and out of the photonic chip.
Researchers can control the direction of the outgoing beam by changing the phase of the light sent to each antenna. Adjusting these phases changes the angle at which the array releases light, making it possible to steer the beam without moving any physical components.
The Antenna Spacing Problem
Placing the antennas close together creates a serious obstacle. Neighboring antennas can couple with one another, scrambling the light they produce. Engineers have traditionally prevented this interference by increasing the distance between antennas, but wider spacing creates a different set of problems.
When antennas are too far apart, the array produces several copies of the same beam at different angles. The primary beam can only be moved a limited distance before it becomes difficult to distinguish from these additional copies.
"This limits our field of view, so the autonomous vehicle now only knows what is in front of it for a certain angular range," Garcia Coleto explains.
The unwanted beam copies, called grating lobes, can confuse the sensor and generate false detections. They also consume energy that could otherwise be directed into the main beam.
To overcome this tradeoff, the MIT researchers developed antennas with reduced crosstalk that can be positioned close together without strongly coupling.
Three Antenna Shapes Reduce Interference
In a conventional OPA, every antenna has an identical structure and uses the same pattern of corrugations. When these matching antennas are placed close together, they interact very strongly.
The MIT team instead created a repeating set of three antennas with distinct shapes. They changed the width of the antennas as well as the size and placement of the corrugations. Because the antennas have different geometries, each one also has a different propagation coefficient, which describes how light moves through the structure.
"Because the antennas have very different propagation coefficients, when we put them close together, essentially each antenna doesn't 'see' the antenna next to it. Therefore, it won't couple with its neighbor," Garcia Coleto says.
Making Different Antennas Behave the Same Way
Reducing the coupling was only part of the challenge. Although the antennas needed different propagation coefficients, they still had to release light in the same consistent manner.
The team designed the antennas around three essential requirements.
Each antenna had to emit the same amount of light. Every antenna also needed to release its beam at the same angle when receiving the same wavelength. Finally, the angle of emission had to change evenly across the entire array as the beam was steered.
"We have this challenge where we require the antennas to have different geometries to reduce the crosstalk, but we need to simultaneously design the antennas to have the same emission characteristics. While it is possible to engineer this, it is extremely difficult because, typically, when antennas are designed with different geometries, they tend to behave differently," Crawford-Eng says.
The researchers began by developing the basic electromagnetic theory describing how radiative modes couple. They then used this theoretical framework to guide the design and computer simulation of the antennas.
Based on those calculations, the team manufactured an OPA containing the reduced-crosstalk antennas. The antennas were placed much closer together than those in a conventional system, and the completed device was then tested experimentally.
Interference Falls From About 100 Percent to 1 Percent
Under the conditions of the experiment, a typical OPA would have produced coupling of approximately 100 percent. The MIT design lowered that coupling to about 1 percent while still generating one clean and precise beam.
The system accurately steered the beam across a broad field of view without producing any grating lobes. This combination of wide scanning, low interference, and strong beam quality addresses one of the central obstacles facing integrated lidar technology.
The researchers now plan to refine the method so the system can cover an even broader viewing range. They are also studying another possible approach to wide field-of-view performance that emerged while they were developing the underlying theory.
"This work addresses a longstanding challenge in integrated optical phased arrays: simultaneously achieving both a wide field of view, which requires dense antenna spacing, and high beam quality, which requires low crosstalk between neighboring antennas. The authors solve this problem with an elegant antenna design. Their innovation is an important step forward for chip-scale, solid-state beam-steering technology," says Joyce Poon, professor of electrical and computer engineering at the University of Toronto and director of the Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, who was not involved with this work.
The Semiconductor Research Corporation, the National Science Foundation, an MIT MathWorks Fellowship, the U.S. Department of War, and the MIT Rolf G. Locher Endowed Fellowship supported the research, in part.
Some of the work was carried out using MIT.nano facilities.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Original written by Adam Zewe. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Henry Crawford-Eng, Andres Garcia Coleto, Benjamin M. Mazur, Daniel M. DeSantis, Tal Sneh, Jelena Notaros. Reduced-crosstalk antennas for grating-lobe-free and wide-field-of-view integrated optical phased arrays. Nature Communications, 2026; 17 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-71832-y

articles.title: GTA 6's "physical" PS5 codes in Japan will expire after 170 days
articles.text:
Facepalm: Grand Theft Auto fans were already upset that GTA 6 will be a digital-only release, with the so-called physical edition containing just a code to download the game. Gamers who purchased the retail box are now expressing even more frustration after it was officially confirmed that PS5 product codes in Japan will expire 170 days after the game's scheduled launch date of November 19, 2026.
Rockstar clarified that the expiration period is only applicable to the PS5 version of the game in Japan and won't affect buyers in the rest of the world. The company also confirmed that codes purchased for the Xbox are not region locked and will not expire, but it did not explain why it's implementing the policy on one platform but not the other.
Explaining the rationale behind the unusual decision, Rockstar said that download codes work differently depending on the platform and country of purchase, and the Japan-specific policy was put in place due to "regulatory restrictions" in the country. The company also recommended that gamers buy from local retailers to avoid potential activation problems.
Following the announcement, many fans took to social media, slamming Rockstar for setting expiration dates on the download codes. While some likened digital gaming to renting rather than owning a product, others wondered whether Rockstar will also introduce a similar policy in other markets. Others joked that the much-hyped digital future looks brighter with every passing day.
It is worth noting that some gamers and social media commentators have speculated that the expiration date may not apply to the actual game, but only to the DLC content, which is available through a separate code in Japan. However, that still does not explain why the policy applies to PS5 but not Xbox. Rockstar has yet to clarify the matter.
GTA VI will launch on November 19, 2026, with the Standard Edition priced at $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition at $99.99. The game will be available only on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S at launch, with no word on whether there will be a PC version in the future. It is currently available for pre-order on the official Rockstar Store, the PlayStation Store, and the Xbox Store.

articles.title: AI enthusiast adds Nvidia Tesla V100 as loud as a lawnmower to gaming PC for $266 — 32GB of VRAM rig can run 27 billion parameter model at 32 tokens per second
articles.text:
AI enthusiast adds Nvidia Tesla V100 as loud as a lawnmower to gaming PC for $266 — 32GB of VRAM rig can run 27 billion parameter model at 32 tokens per second
Now they have a total 32GB VRAM system on a budget, for local LLM inference.
A computing enthusiast has repurposed a very noisy and largely obsolete enterprise GPU (with lots of VRAM) for local LLM inference purposes. They are now enjoying a system that has doubled its total VRAM quota to 32GB for just a $266 (£200) outlay. That’s a good result, especially in the midst of a RAMpocalypse.
Oscar Molnar explains that a cheap Tesla V100 SXM2 with 16GB HBM2 was sourced, as was an SXM2-to-PCIe adapter, and a PWM mod for the loud-as-a-lawnmower cooler, to complete this VRAM expansion for the hefty local LLMs project. Indeed, these GPUs do look cheap right now, as I can see them listed on eBay US for under $140 each, if you don’t mind buying from China.
As mentioned above, you can’t just get one of these Tesla V100 SXM2 cards with abundant VRAM and plug it into your PC. Molnar says they spent about $66 on an SXM2-to-PCIe adapter, also on eBay.
You might think that was enough. However, the PC and local LLMs enthusiast baulked at the noise of “the fan from hell,” which came as standard with the Tesla V100 SXM2. That shrieking cooler was measured outputting 82dB of noise. Molnar described it as “somewhere between a garbage disposal and a lawnmower.” This may be the most complicated tweak yet, but basically the existing fan wires just needed rerouting and plugging into the motherboard PWM fan header. You could also simply purchase a “2.54mm male to PH2.0 female jumper cable” for the task. Apparently, the fan only needs to run at 10% to keep the Tesla V100 under 50C at full load.
27 billion parameter LLM runs at 32 tokens per second
With the hardware all now fitted and finessed, Molnar had a 32GB VRAM system at their disposal – that’s a PC with RTX 4080: 16GB VRAM, Ada architecture and Tesla V100: 16GB VRAM, Volta architecture. They note you can get Tesla V100s with 32GB of VRAM, but they are double the price.
Getting the system to make use of this 32GB of total VRAM for LLMs wasn’t tricky, says the DIYer. They used NixOS with a legacy Nvidia driver that overlapped support for both Volta and Ada architectures. Testing a local LLM, they got a 27 billion parameter model running at 32 tokens per second, which they say is “fast enough for interactive use” and faster than most cloud API alternatives.

articles.title: CEO do Hugging Face pede "transparência radical" após ataque da OpenAI
articles.text:
Após a OpenAI admitir que um de seus modelos invadiu os sistemas da plataforma Hugging Face, o CEO da empresa, Clem Delangue, publicou no X que viajaria a São Francisco (EUA) para ter “uma pequena conversa com aquele ‘agente rebelde'”. Em seguida, num post publicado no sábado (25), ele detalhou o que pediu à OpenAI.
A principal demanda é o que Delangue chamou de “transparência radical”: que a OpenAI libere os registros de atividade dos agentes envolvidos no ataque para que “toda a comunidade de pesquisa possa estudar o que aconteceu”.
Além disso, ele pediu que a empresa destine US$ 100 milhões (R$ 508,3 milhões) em poder computacional para ajudar a comunidade da Hugging Face a construir defesas cibernéticas usando modelos abertos e fechados.
Leia mais:
- Aprenda a usar o ChatGPT: 10 dicas valiosas para criar perguntas precisas
- Como melhorar seu texto no ChatGPT: guia prático do básico ao avançado
- OpenAI percebeu que o ChatGPT invadiu sistema do Hugging Face dias depois
“O primeiro ciberataque por agente autônomo é um evento inédito. Ele merece uma resposta inédita!”, escreveu Delangue.
Apesar do caráter autônomo do ataque, especialistas em cibersegurança apontaram que ele também pode ser atribuído a erro humano — especificamente, a uma falha aparente da OpenAI em configurar corretamente o que deveria ser um ambiente de testes completamente isolado.
EUA debatem lei de emergência após inteligência artificial escapar de contenção
Nesta quinta-feira (23), Washington (EUA) tornou-se o centro de uma mobilização legislativa e executiva. A reação ocorreu logo após a OpenAI confirmar que um de seus agentes autônomos ultrapassou os limites de isolamento durante um ensaio de segurança e invadiu a estrutura digital da startup Hugging Face.
O incidente acionou o alarme no primeiro escalão norte-americano. Diante da gravidade do episódio, o conselheiro tecnológico da Casa Branca, Michael Kratsios, passou a acompanhar a evolução do caso, enquanto parlamentares no Capitólio passaram a desenhar respostas regulatórias urgentes para conter riscos cibernéticos globais.
Leia a matéria completa aqui
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Lo que debes ver para disfrutar mejor ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
articles.text:
Avengers: Doomsday promete no solo ser uno de los grandes estrenos del año 2026. También, romper la taquilla y demostrar que, a pesar de sus momentos bajos, el Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel continúa siendo uno de los más rentables del mundo. Y por ahora, parece que todo apunta a que cualquier previsión se quedará corta. Apenas a días de su estreno, ya la preventa de boletos en Norteamérica rompió récords. Un éxito que también se reflejó en las visualizaciones del tráiler, convertido en uno de los más vistos de Marvel en su historia.
Por supuesto, razones no faltan. Avengers: Doomsday de los hermanos Russo es la producción más ambiciosa de La casa de las ideas. Especialmente, después de años de progresiva erosión de la franquicia. Pero para Kevin Feige la cosa está clara: la cinta es tanto una demostración de fuerza como la oportunidad ideal de celebrar lo mejor de la saga. Además, refundar las bases para la siguiente fase, que el mismo productor ya anunció sería algo por completo nuevo y sin duda, más sencillo que la actual.
Pero mientras eso ocurre, Avengers: Doomsday se enfrenta a un problema habitual en el Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel. La de unir los puntos entre las diversas producciones, personajes e historias, de cara a la nueva cinta. Lo que, claro está, plantea la habitual pregunta de qué ver para entender mejor la futura historia en la pantalla grande. Si te lo estás preguntando, este artículo es para ti. Te dejamos todo lo que debes ver para disfrutar mejor Avengers: Doomsday. Lo que incluye una querida serie dedicada a un personaje insigne, pasando por todo lo que hay que saber sobre el multiverso. Un viaje emocionante para despedir una etapa de una de las grandes franquicias del cine.
Un recorrido multiversal para ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
Por supuesto, un elemento central de Avengers: Doomsday es el concepto del multiverso y sus ramificaciones. Mucho más, las reglas que el Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel elaboró a lo largo de casi un lustro para entender el concepto. En específico, porque de la misma manera que en el mundo del cómic, las realidades alternativas exploran la capacidad de las historias para reinventarlo. Algo que incluye, desde personajes con diferentes variantes, hasta universos paralelos que podrían interactuar en la ambiciosa producción.
De modo que la producción televisiva más crucial para entender la idea es la serie de Disney+, Loki. Las temporadas 1 y 2 de la historia del dios de la travesura interpretado por Tom Hiddleston, de hecho, sostienen buena parte de la idea de la Saga del Multiverso. En la trama se explica el funcionamiento de la Sagrada Línea Temporal, la Autoridad de Variación Temporal (TVA) y cómo Loki termina sosteniendo las realidades para evitar el colapso absoluto. Luego de la breve aparición del asgardiano en el tráiler de Avengers: Doomsday, es más que obvio que su participación será central.
Por otro lado, a nivel cinematográfico, es obligatorio ver Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021) y Doctor Strange en el multiverso de la locura (2022). Ambas cintas introducen de manera práctica las consecuencias de alterar las realidades alternas. Y además, desarrollan formalmente el concepto de las incursiones. Este último, el devastador fenómeno físico donde dos universos colisionan entre sí destruyéndose mutuamente. Un peligro cósmico que servirá como el detonante principal de la trama de Avengers: Doomsday.
En especial, Doctor Strange en el multiverso de la locura indaga en cuál es el trasfondo de la naturaleza de las realidades paralelas. Un recorrido vertiginoso que lleva al mismísimo Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch) a recorrer varios universos distintos. La trama, además, muestra diferentes versiones de personajes conocidos. Además, la forma en que esa existencia puede determinar todo un nuevo sentido de sus poderes y capacidades. Un tema que es evidente, la venidera cinta de Marvel tocará y que permitirá entender las profundas implicaciones del tiempo y el espacio escindido.
Un paseo por los personajes más memorables de Marvel
Otro de los puntos esenciales para comprender Avengers: Doomsday es la caótica colisión de realidades y la forma en que interactuarán los personajes. Por lo que Deadpool & Wolverine (Lobezno) de 2024 es vital. Todo debido a que su trama absorbe al viejo universo de mutantes de la extinta 20th Century Fox. Un giro que termina por incluirlas dentro de la continuidad oficial del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel. Además, la cinta explica cómo los personajes pueden sobrevivir a la degradación de sus respectivas líneas de origen.
Asimismo, resulta imprescindible ver Los 4 Fantásticos: Primeros pasos (2025). Eso, al introducir al legendario equipo compuesto por Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby), Johnny Storm (Joseph Quinn) y Ben Grimm (Ebon Moss-Bachrach). Estos, habitando en una realidad alternativa de estética retrofuturista. Comprender la procedencia de este equipo cósmico es elemental, en especial, debido a que el contexto de Los 4 Fantásticos servirá como el nexo directo hacia el villano central. Y además, que su escena postcréditos vincula de forma directa las motivaciones del antagonista definitivo. A saber, el clásico Doctor Doom interpretado por Robert Downey Jr.
Pero además, la cinta de la clásica familia de Marvel muestra la forma en que una realidad alternativa puede ser por completo independiente de la central. En el caso del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel, la Tierra-616. Hasta ahora, las diferentes conexiones entre el multiverso parecían conectadas por las variantes de los héroes de la Tierra o, en cualquier caso, sus antecesores. Sin embargo, en Los 4 Fantásticos: Primeros pasos, los icónicos héroes son los únicos en su mundo. Lo que demuestra las posibilidades ilimitadas del concepto multiversal.
¿Y quiénes defenderán la Tierra? Para saberlo, debes ver estas películas y series
Para entender quiénes defenderán la Tierra en el frente principal, es necesario repasar lo ocurrido después de Avengers: Endgame. Por lo que Capitán América: Brave New World (2025) es una de las opciones más importantes. Todo debido a que Sam Wilson (Anthony Mackie) asume por completo el manto del Capitán América.
Si deseas explorar cómo llegamos a ese punto, por supuesto tendrás que ver Falcon y el Soldado de Invierno (2021). Pero en esencia, la cinta que continúa la historia es suficiente, al narrar cómo el héroe intenta reconstruir activamente un nuevo equipo de Vengadores. Eso, en medio de un entorno geopolítico fragmentado y hostil.
Otra película esencial es Thunderbolts* (2025). En especial, porque la trama presenta a Los Nuevos Vengadores. El equipo liderado por Yelena (Florence Pugh), John Walker (Wyatt Russell) y Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan) tendrá un papel preponderante en Avengers: Doomsday. Pero además presenta a Sentry (Lewis Pullman), uno de los héroes recientes más poderosos de Marvel. Y probablemente, el que tendrá un peso esencial en la futura trama de Avengers: Doomsday.
Un mundo nuevo después de Thanos en ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
Claro está, la geografía política global de la Tierra y sus alianzas secretas también jugarán un rol preponderante ante la batalla multiversal. En especial, lo que ha ocurrido en el mundo después del blip de Avengers: Endgame. Para comenzar, es necesario darle una nueva revisión a Black Panther: Wakanda Forever (2022). Esta, una cinta esencial que redefine el balance de poder en el planeta. La trama no solo detalla la transición de Shuri (Letitia Wright) como la nueva Pantera Negra tras la muerte de su hermano, T’Challa (Chadwick Boseman).
A la vez, introduce formalmente al mutante Namor (Ténoch Huerta) y su reino submarino de Talokan. El tráiler de Avengers: Doomsday confirma que los wakandianos y la armada de Talokan formarán una de las facciones clave en la resistencia contra Doom. Además, incluye en tu lista Shang-Chi y la leyenda de los Diez Anillos (2021), que te dará contexto sobre el héroe asiático y te recordará su interesante historia.
Pero sin duda, hay dos cintas que te ayudarán a entender el mundo en el que conviven todos los nuevos personajes del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel. Avengers: Infinity War (2018) y Avengers: Endgame (2019). Pero en especial, el giro asombroso de incluir a Robert Downey Jr. como Doom. Claro está, el villano es un personaje originario de otra realidad y no una versión corrupta de Iron Man. Aun así, es evidente que el hecho de que el actor encarne a ambos tiene su peso.
En específico, al poner el rostro del hombre que se sacrificó para salvar al universo en el del tirano que ahora busca destruirlo. Lo que ya se considera un juego de metaficción brutal. Eso, a pesar de que todavía no está del todo claro si el parecido físico tendrá implicaciones. Pero incluso, de no tenerlas, el paralelismo entre ambos personajes será esencial. Lo que solo podrá entenderse a cabalidad a través de ambas cintas.

articles.title: Carrie is just trying to make a friend in the new trailer
articles.text:
Mike Flanagan’s latest Stephen King adaptation, Carrie (this will be his fourth), is slated to make its debut on Amazon Prime on October 7th. The new trailer dropped at Comic-Con 2026 and doesn’t contain many surprises. If you’re familiar with Carrie at all, it hits all the expected notes. Though it’s clearly been updated for the modern era.
Carrie is just trying to make a friend in the new trailer
Mike Flanagan’s adaptation updates the Stephen King classic for the modern age.
Mike Flanagan’s adaptation updates the Stephen King classic for the modern age.
According to Deadline, Flanagan’s take on the classic King novel will tackle very modern teen challenges like active shooter drills and bullying on social media. The director apparently invited high schoolers into the writers’ room, using their real-life traumas to inform the script:
“They shared shocking one-off situations or constant treatment and microaggressions and things that are not necessarily present themselves as targeted harassment. [We will dive into] the cruelty in today’s world and how the internet has encouraged cruelty, rewards and celebrates and amplifies it. This is awful for adults to deal with, and for teenagers even more so.”
Brian De Palma’s iconic 1976 adaptation of Carrie is iconic and features an unimpeachable performance from Sissy Spacek. But it’s undeniable that Summer H. Howell, who was 21 at the time of shooting, is much more believable as a high school student than Spacek, who was 26 at the time.

articles.title: Taxe sur les petits colis : attention, les pirates pourraient s'en servir pour vous piéger
articles.text:
La taxe douanière européenne de 3 euros sur les petits colis est officiellement entrée en vigueur. De leur côté, certains arnaqueurs multiplient les arnaques au colis non livré ou bloqué à la douane. Justement, la société de cybersécurité Bitdefender craint que des escrocs mobilisent la nouvelle taxe douanière européenne pour piéger leurs victimes. Mais de quelle façon ? Avant toute chose, revenons brièvement sur le fonctionnement de cette nouvelle taxe européenne.
Rappel du fonctionnement de la taxe européenne sur les petits colis
Depuis ce 1er juillet, la taxe douanière européenne de 3 euros sur les colis expédiés depuis des pays hors de l’UE est entrée en vigueur. Son objectif : freiner l’afflux de colis provenant de plateformes d’e-commerce extra-européennes, comme Shein, Temu ou AliExpress. Plus précisément, cette taxe concerne les colis de moins de 150 euros et elle ne s’applique pas par colis, mais par catégorie de produit. Par exemple, un colis contenant un t-shirt, une coque de smartphone et un jouet sera soumis à trois taxes forfaitaires, vu qu’il contient trois catégories de produits différentes. À l’inverse, un colis contenant trois t-shirts ne sera taxé qu’une seule fois, puisqu’il ne comporte qu’une seule catégorie de produits. Au passage, rappelons que le gouvernement français a abandonné son projet de taxe de 2 euros sur les petits colis afin de ne conserver que le dispositif européen.
Les arnaqueurs pourraient utiliser cette taxe européenne pour piéger leurs victimes
Cela ne vous a sans doute pas échappé, mais les arnaqueurs ont souvent recours à des histoires de colis non livré pour piéger leurs victimes. Justement, la société de cybersécurité Bitdefender alerte sur les possibilités d’arnaques liées à cette nouvelle taxe douanière européenne. À l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, aucun cas n’a été recensé, mais il vaut mieux prévenir que guérir. Quelle forme pourrait prendre cette arnaque ? On peut facilement imaginer un escroc envoyer un message à sa victime indiquant : « Votre colis est retenu en attente de paiement ». Le tout accompagné du logo d’une administration douanière ou d’une institution officielle, ainsi que d’un texte généré par l’IA évoquant la nouvelle taxe douanière européenne, afin de rendre l’arnaque plus crédible.
Le message inciterait la victime à régler un petit montant (par exemple 3 euros, comme la véritable taxe douanière européenne) afin de débloquer un colis prétendument retenu à la douane. En fin de compte, la victime se retrouverait face à un formulaire frauduleux programmé pour enregistrer les données confidentielles saisies (nom, coordonnées, numéro de carte bancaire, cryptogramme, etc.).
Comment ne pas tomber dans le piège ?
Si vous recevez un message vous indiquant qu’un colis est bloqué à la douane, la meilleure chose à faire est de consulter la plateforme du transporteur et de vous fier seulement aux informations qui s’y trouvent. Par ailleurs, si vous n’attendez aucun colis, il s’agit probablement d’une arnaque. Dans tous les cas, méfiez-vous de tout SMS, e-mail ou QR code vous invitant à régler des frais de douane. Méfiez-vous également des données personnelles précises qui peuvent être indiquées dans un message. Les arnaqueurs exploitent désormais des bases de données issues de fuites de données pour rendre leurs arnaques plus crédibles. Par ailleurs, les arnaqueurs perfectionnent régulièrement leurs arnaques au colis non livré. À titre d’exemple, l’arnaque ci-dessous intègre une photo, ainsi qu’un message audio provenant soi-disant du livreur.
Plus généralement, les arnaqueurs ont tendance à se servir de l’actualité ou d’une période spécifique de l’année pour parvenir à leurs fins. C’est notamment le cas des faux climatiseurs, qui se sont multipliés durant cet été caniculaire, ou encore de l’arnaque au péage, particulièrement fréquentes pendant les périodes des départs en vacances. Une arnaque mobilisant la taxe européenne sur les petits colis a donc des chances de voir le jour.

articles.title: What is AI Leadership? Exploring Key Skills, Qualifications & Career Pathways - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence isn’t just changing how we work. It’s also changing who’s expected to lead.
Companies across Australia are putting a lot of money into AI, but just bringing in new technology isn’t enough. Someone still needs to figure out where AI fits, how to use it responsibly, and whether it’s actually solving the problems it was meant to fix. That’s what AI leadership is about.
But AI leaders aren’t always the people coding or building machine learning models all day. A lot of the time, they’re the ones who connect technical teams, business leaders, and regular employees to make sure AI is used in a practical, ethical, and genuinely helpful way.
So what does that actually involve?
Building The Right Foundation
There’s no single path to becoming an AI leader, but having a good grasp of both technology and business definitely helps a lot. For those wanting to move into these roles, enrolling in a postgraduate degree in AI leadership can be especially useful.
These programs don’t just focus on coding or data science. They cover everything ranging from how AI fits into real companies, including strategy, governance, ethics, managing risks, and leading teams through tech changes. And as time goes on, this mix is becoming more important because Australian businesses need people who can marry their technical skills with business decisions.
Of course, you don’t have to study formally to learn this stuff. Lots of people pick it up through work experience. But having a structured background can give you a clearer view of the big picture, especially if you want to move into senior leadership eventually.
Understanding People Matters Just As Much As Understanding Technology
Most people think that AI leadership is all about tech. Sure, tech is a huge part of it, but it’s not the only thing that matters. A lot of the time the bigger challenge usually involves people.
New AI systems often change how teams work, which can make some employees nervous. Some worry about their jobs, and others don’t understand why things have to change in the first place. A good AI leader can explain these changes transparently and clearly. They listen to concerns, answer questions honestly, and help people adjust without leaving them behind.
That’s why communication is just as important as technical know-how. If people don’t trust the leader, even the best AI systems will struggle to gain traction.
Knowing When AI Shouldn’t Be Used
It’s incredibly easy to get excited about AI, especially with so many new tools coming out all the time. But a strong AI leader also knows when not to use AI. Not every process needs automation, and not every decision should be made by an algorithm. Sometimes a simple spreadsheet, a straightforward workflow, or a conversation between two people will do the job perfectly well.
Good leaders ask practical questions before starting. Will this really save time? Will it make the customer experience better? Are there privacy issues? Does the business have good data to support this? Sometimes the answer is yes. Sometimes it’s a no. Knowing the difference is what separates careful leadership from just jumping on the latest trend for the sake of it.
Ethics Aren’t Just A Buzzword
Artificial intelligence can process enormous amounts of information, that’s for sure. But that doesn’t automatically make every outcome fair or accurate.
AI systems are only as good as the data they’re trained on. The better the data, the more accurate the output will be. But if that training data contains any kind of bias or gaps, then the result will reflect exactly that. That’s why ethical decision-making has become such an important part of AI leadership.
In Australia, organisations are paying much closer attention to privacy, transparency, and accountability than they were even a few years ago. Customers, employees, and regulators all expect businesses to explain how AI is being used and what safeguards are in place.
Good leaders don’t treat ethics as some box-ticking exercise. They build those conversations into the planning process from day one.
Staying Curious Is Part Of The Job
It takes a certain level of curiosity to work with a constantly changing field like AI. New tools and techniques seem to pop up almost overnight. Old ones get updated all the time. Regulations evolve, research moves quickly, and what feels novel today can become standard practice (or even stale) surprisingly fast.
This doesn’t mean that an AI leader has to be an expert at everything. What it does mean, however, is that leaders should stay curious and on top of what’s happening in the field. Reading about what’s new, proactively attending industry events, and listening to experts’ insights are just a few of the many ways to build confidence in your knowledge.
Remember, it’s not about chasing every trend. It’s more about having a general idea of what’s out there, so you can make sensible decisions when new opportunities come along.
Career Opportunities Continue To Grow
A few years ago, AI jobs mostly meant working for tech companies. That’s changing pretty fast. Today, you can find AI popping up in almost every industry.
It’s being used by hospitals to help analyse scans. Banks are getting better at detecting fraud with AI tools. Manufacturers are finding ways to make production lines more efficient, and retailers are using it to better understand what customers really want. Even local councils and government departments are starting to look at where AI can save time or improve services.
Because of this, the people who have the skills and ability to lead these projects are becoming just as valuable as the people building the technology itself. And the interesting thing is, a lot of those jobs don’t even mention AI in the title.
Project managers, department heads, operations managers, tech professionals and business leaders are all finding themselves involved in AI projects, whether they expected to or not. It’s slowly becoming one of those skills that’s useful almost everywhere, not just in technology.
Leading Successful AI Adoption
AI leadership isn’t about being the smartest person in the room. It’s about understanding enough to ask good questions, make sensible decisions, and help everyone else get the best out of the technology without losing sight of the people using it.
As AI becomes part of everyday work across Australia, organisations will need more people who can bridge the technical side with the human side. That’s probably the biggest challenge going forward, but that’s also what makes AI leadership such an interesting career path.
The technology will change, but helping people adapt to it will always be the part that matters most.

articles.title: iPhone pliant, randonnée mal indiquée sur Google Maps, incendies – le récap’ tech de la semaine - Numerama
articles.text:
Oups, Apple vient de confirmer que l’iPhone pliant arrive très bientôt
- La bêta 4 d’iOS 27 a accidentellement révélé l’existence d’un futur iPhone avec deux batteries, probablement destiné à un modèle pliant.
- Les messages d’erreur dans le code iOS mentionnent des problèmes pouvant affecter plusieurs batteries dans un même appareil, confirmant indirectement un nouveau design de smartphone.
- Un lancement officiel de cet iPhone pliant est anticipé pour septembre, coïncidant avec le calendrier de sortie habituel d’Apple, malgré un possible report.
Google Maps annonçait 5 heures pour cette randonnée de 14 heures : les secours ont dû intervenir
- Google Maps a évalué à 5 h 13 une section du Howe Sound Crest Trail qui en demande 12 à 14, selon Lions Bay Search and Rescue.
- Conçue pour la ville, l’application ne modélise ni le dénivelé, ni les passages techniques, ni les conditions, rendant ses estimations en terrain alpin trompeuses.
- Les secouristes recommandent des apps spécialisées (AllTrails, Granite, Gaia GPS, Avenza) et rappellent qu’elles ne remplacent pas une préparation rigoureuse.
Incendies à Biscarrosse, en Gironde et ailleurs en France : Google Maps aide à suivre la localisation des feux en direct
- La saison des feux 2026 en France bat tous les records, avec 46 000 hectares déjà brûlés.
- Google Maps propose un calque « Feux de forêt » pour visualiser en direct les périmètres des brasiers et les routes fermées, sur mobile comme sur web.
- Ce suivi s’appuie sur des données satellites (Copernicus, NOAA) traitées par l’IA, mises à jour plusieurs fois par jour et capables de déclencher des notifications d’évitement.

articles.title: Internet aus 18 km Höhe: Dieser Helium-Ballon fliegt im August nach Japan
articles.text:
Dieser 60-Meter-Ballon soll Internet aus der Stratosphäre liefern
Die Flugroute ist ganz beachtlich: Im August soll sich der „Silberpfeil“ seinen Weg durch die trockene Luft im Südwesten der USA bahnen und schließlich den Pazifik überqueren. Die Küste Japans soll das Ziel sein – allerdings nicht das Land. Die an ein Luftschiff erinnernde Flugplattform wird etwa 18 Kilometer über der Meeresoberfläche in der Stratosphäre stationiert. Mithilfe einer speziell angefertigten Antenne soll die circa 60 Meter lange Plattform von dort aus das 5G-Netz von Softbank ergänzen – ein Test, bei dem Daten direkt an Geräte übertragen werden sollen.
Internet und Fernerkundung: Der Einsatz der Flugplattformen ist vielfältig
Ausgedacht hat sich das Unterfangen das in New Mexico ansässige Unternehmen Sceye (ausgesprochen wie das englische Wort „sky“). Es ist mit seinem Konzept nicht allein. Mehrere Unternehmen arbeiten daran, eine Klasse von Luftfahrzeugen namens HAPS zu entwickeln. Die Abkürzung steht für „High-Altitude Platform Stations“. Eine solche Plattform kann ein Flugzeug, ein Ballon oder eben ein längliches, mit Helium gefülltes und mit Solarpaneelen ausgestattetes Fluggerät sein. HAPS-Unternehmen, darunter die Airbus-Tochter Aalto, sehen ihre Fluggeräte für eine Vielzahl von Zwecken in der Luft, wie beispielsweise der Bereitstellung von Internetdiensten an Katastrophenorten und der Beobachtung der Erdoberfläche.
Die Stratosphäre ist ein guter Ort, wenn man ein großes Gebiet abdecken möchte. Sie ist unterhalb der Satelliten, die in der niedrigsten Umlaufbahn unterwegs sind. Das bedeutet, dass das Senden eines Signals weitaus weniger Energie erfordert. „Was wir letztendlich bieten, sind weltraumähnliche Bedingungen – ohne die Kosten einer Weltraumfahrt und ohne die Komplexität eines Aufenthalts in der Umlaufbahn“, sagt Mikkel Vestergaard Frandsen, CEO und Gründer von Sceye.
Die Bedingungen in der Stratosphäre
Aber es ist gar nicht so einfach, in der Stratosphäre zu bleiben. Das Fluggerät von Sceye, so Frandsen, muss leicht genug sein, um in der Luft zu bleiben, aber auch stabil genug, um die notwendigen Systeme zu tragen. Es muss tagsüber genügend Sonnenenergie aufnehmen und speichern, um rund um die Uhr Strom für Rotoren zu liefern. Die sind dazu da, das HAPS wieder in Position zu bringen, wenn Winde es aus der Bahn werfen – eine Fähigkeit, die das Sceye-HAPS bei einem Testflug im Jahr 2024 unter Beweis gestellt hat.
Seitdem bereitet sich Sceye auf seinen großen Test in Japan vor. Bei einem Test in diesem Frühjahr beispielsweise blieb das Fluggerät zwölf Tage lang in der Luft, während es zur Küste Brasiliens flog. Mehr als 88 Stunden verbrachte es fest an verschiedenen Orten. Letztendlich möchte das Unternehmen, dass seine Plattform Satellitenbetreibern hilft, dicht besiedelte Gebiete besser mit einem Internetzugang zu versorgen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 13.07.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.
